title: Things to Do in Sonamarg: Thajiwas Glacier, Zoji La & the Great Lakes
seoTitle: Things to Do in Sonamarg: Glacier, Treks & Views | Kudozz Club
description: Things to do in Sonamarg: the pony ride or walk to Thajiwas Glacier, sledging on summer snow, the Sindh river, rafting and trout fishing, the drive to Zoji La, Baltal, the Kashmir Great Lakes trek and Nilagrad.
dek: The meadow of gold on the road to Ladakh, where glaciers come down almost to the road and the Sindh river runs through pine forest.
searchIntent: Travellers visiting Sonamarg on a day trip from Srinagar or staying a night on the way to Ladakh or a trek.

hero.alt: Snowfield and pine forest on the trail to Thajiwas Glacier
hero.caption: Trail to Thajiwas Glacier

intro: Sonamarg, at about 2,800 metres in Ganderbal district, is around 80 km north-east of Srinagar on the highway to Ladakh. The name means meadow of gold, and in summer the valley of the Sindh river is lined with meadows, birch and pine, with glaciers hanging off the peaks above.

The main things to do in Sonamarg are the pony ride or walk to Thajiwas Glacier, time by the river, and, for the adventurous, the drive to Zoji La or the start of the Kashmir Great Lakes trek. It is also close to Baltal, the base camp for the shorter Amarnath Yatra route.
Sonamarg is usually visited as a day trip from Srinagar or for one night. The Z-Morh (Sonamarg) tunnel, opened in 2025, has improved winter access, but services in winter are still limited.
quickAnswer: Ride a pony or walk to Thajiwas Glacier
Go sledging on the glacier snow in summer
Drive up to Zoji La (with permits and conditions)
See Baltal, the Amarnath base camp
Start the Kashmir Great Lakes trek
Fish for trout with a permit

items.name: Ride or walk to Thajiwas Glacier
body: The Thajiwas Glacier lies a few kilometres from the Sonamarg taxi stand, up a side valley ringed by peaks. Most visitors ride ponies; the walk takes about an hour each way on a gentle but rough path. Snow usually lingers at the glacier's foot well into summer.
Pony-wallahs have fixed rates listed by the local authorities; check the board and agree on the route (and whether it includes waiting time) before you set off.

items.name: Go sledging on summer snow
body: At the snowfield below the glacier, local sledge-pullers offer rides down the slope. It is a highlight for children and first-time snow visitors. Wear shoes with grip and avoid going onto the glacier itself or under overhanging ice.

items.name: Walk along the Sindh
body: The Sindh river flows past Sonamarg through meadows and forest. Short walks along the bank give quiet views away from the busy main stretch of the highway.

items.name: Try rafting
body: Rafting on the Sindh runs in the warmer months on stretches near Sonamarg and further downstream, with moderate rapids. Go with registered operators.

items.name: Fish for trout
body: The Sindh and its side streams have brown and rainbow trout. Permits from the fisheries department are required for designated beats.

items.name: Drive to Zoji La

image.alt: Valley view from the road to Zoji La
image.caption: The road to Zoji La

body: Zoji La, at about 3,500 metres, is the pass between Kashmir and Ladakh, about 15 km beyond Baltal. The road is narrow and unpaved in places, with sheer drops, and snow walls in early summer. Sonamarg taxis run trips to Zero Point beyond the pass. Access depends on conditions and traffic rules; check before you go.

items.name: See Baltal
body: Baltal, about 15 km from Sonamarg, is the base camp for the shorter route to the Amarnath cave shrine. During the yatra in July and August it becomes a large tent city; the rest of the summer it is a quiet valley.

items.name: Trek the Kashmir Great Lakes

image.alt: Krishansar Lake on the Kashmir Great Lakes trek
image.caption: Krishansar Lake

body: The Kashmir Great Lakes trek begins near Sonamarg and crosses high passes past a chain of turquoise lakes including Vishansar, Krishansar, Gadsar and Gangbal before ending at Naranag. It takes about seven days and is one of the most beautiful treks in India. Go with a registered operator.

items.name: Walk to Nilagrad
body: Nilagrad, a short drive from Sonamarg, is a stream whose reddish water is locally believed to have healing properties. It is a quiet stop with views of the valley.

items.name: Summer (May to September)
body: The meadows are green, Thajiwas has summer snow for sledging, and the Great Lakes trek is open from July. It is the main season, and the highway to Ladakh is busy with trucks, bikers and pilgrims.

facts.Best time: June and September for fewer crowds

items.name: Autumn (October to November)
body: The birches and meadows turn golden and the crowds thin out. Nights are cold, and early snow can close Zoji La.

items.name: Winter (December to March)
body: Sonamarg is under deep snow. With the tunnel, it has become possible to visit in winter for snow play and skiing trials, but facilities are limited and weather can close roads. Only go with confirmed accommodation and local advice.

facts.Good to know: Check road status before setting out

byTraveller.text: Leave early, ride to Thajiwas, enjoy the snow and a riverside lunch, and head back before dark.
Stay a night in Sonamarg before crossing Zoji La towards Drass and Kargil to acclimatise.
Sonamarg is the start of the Great Lakes trek; arrive a day early to acclimatise.

oneDay: Drive from Srinagar early along the Sindh. Ride or walk to Thajiwas Glacier and go sledging on the snow. After lunch, drive to Baltal or towards Zoji La if conditions allow, and walk by the river before returning to Srinagar.
tips: Sonamarg is about 80 km from Srinagar, a drive of around three hours.
Outside taxis may be restricted beyond a point; local taxi and pony unions operate here.
Carry warm layers and rain gear; the weather changes quickly.
Ladakh-bound travellers should acclimatise gradually after crossing Zoji La.

faqs.q: What are the best things to do in Sonamarg?
faqs.a: Ride or walk to Thajiwas Glacier, go sledging on the snow, walk by the Sindh river, try rafting, drive to Zoji La and Baltal, and start the Kashmir Great Lakes trek.

faqs.q: Can Sonamarg be done as a day trip from Srinagar?
faqs.a: Yes. It is about three hours each way, so leave early.
Access has improved with the Z-Morh tunnel, but heavy snow can still close roads and many services shut in winter. Check before you go.

faqs.q: How far is Zoji La from Sonamarg?
faqs.a: About 30 km, via Baltal. The road is rough and conditions depend on weather.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Sonamarg?
faqs.a: May to October, when the meadows are green and the glacier and passes are accessible. June and September are less crowded than peak summer.
